questions.question: Which of the following best describes who creates computing innovations?

options.A: Only professional software engineers at large technology companies
options.B: Only government agencies with approved computing budgets
options.C: People create computing innovations
options.D: Only university researchers with advanced degrees in computer science

questions.explanation: People create computing innovations. This is a foundational principle — computing innovations are the result of human creativity and effort across all backgrounds and contexts.

questions.question: A social media platform was originally designed for college students to connect with classmates. It is now used by billions of people worldwide for news, business, and political campaigns. Which of the following best describes this situation?

options.A: The platform has a logic error because it is being used incorrectly
options.B: Computing innovations can be used in ways that their creators had not originally intended
options.C: The platform's creators deliberately planned for all these use cases from the beginning
options.D: The platform should be shut down because it is being misused

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can be used in ways that their creators had not originally intended. Rapid sharing of a program or running it with a large number of users can result in significant impacts beyond the intended purpose or control of the programmer.

questions.question: A single effect of a computing innovation can be viewed as both beneficial and harmful. Which of the following best illustrates this?

options.A: A word processor that helps some users write faster but not others
options.B: GPS navigation that helps drivers find routes efficiently but also enables constant location tracking that raises privacy concerns
options.C: A program with both a free version and a paid version
options.D: A computing innovation that works on some devices but not others

questions.explanation: A single effect can be viewed as both beneficial and harmful by different people or even the same person. GPS location tracking helps navigation (beneficial) but also enables surveillance (harmful).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the responsibility of programmers regarding unintended uses of their computing innovations?

options.A: Programmers are fully responsible for all unintended uses of their programs
options.B: Programmers are not responsible for any unintended uses since they cannot predict them
options.C: Responsible programmers try to consider unintended uses and potential harmful effects, though it is not possible to consider all possible uses
options.D: Programmers must submit their programs to government review before release to prevent misuse

questions.explanation: Responsible programmers try to consider the unintended ways their computing innovations can be used and the potential beneficial and harmful effects. However, it is not possible for a programmer to consider all the ways a computing innovation can be used.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a computing innovation having an unintended beneficial effect?

options.A: A calculator app that crashes when dividing by zero
options.B: Internet communication tools originally developed for military use that later enabled global commerce and social connection
options.C: A video game that is more popular than its creators expected
options.D: A program that runs slower on older hardware than the developers planned

questions.explanation: Computing innovations have often had unintended beneficial effects by leading to advances in other fields. Technologies developed for one purpose often enable unexpected positive applications in other areas.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why not every effect of a computing innovation is anticipated in advance?

options.A: Programmers are not required to think about effects beyond the intended purpose
options.B: Computing innovations are too complex for anyone to fully understand
options.C: The ways people use and interact with innovations are diverse and unpredictable — especially as the number of users grows and the innovation is used in new contexts
options.D: Computing innovations change their own code over time producing unplanned effects

questions.explanation: Not every effect of a computing innovation is anticipated in advance. The diversity of users and contexts, combined with rapid sharing and large numbers of users, can result in significant impacts beyond the intended purpose or control of the programmer.

questions.stimulus: A company develops a targeted advertising algorithm to help businesses show relevant ads to potential customers. After deployment, the algorithm is found to show higher-paying job ads primarily to men and to charge higher prices on certain products to users in lower-income zip codes.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes this situation?

options.A: The algorithm is working correctly because it is maximizing profit for the businesses
options.B: Computing innovations can be used in ways that have harmful impacts on society even when the original purpose was beneficial
options.C: This is not a computing concern because advertising decisions are a business matter
options.D: The algorithm has a syntax error that must be corrected

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can be used in ways that their creators had not intended. Some of these ways can have a harmful impact on society, the economy, or culture. Targeted advertising was designed to help businesses but can be misused at individual and aggregate levels.

questions.stimulus: A company develops a targeted advertising algorithm to help businesses show relevant ads to potential customers. After deployment, the algorithm is found to show higher-paying job ads primarily to men and to charge higher prices on certain products to users in lower-income zip codes.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes what responsible programmers should do to address situations like this?

options.A: Wait for users to report problems before taking any action
options.B: Try to consider the unintended ways their computing innovations can be used and the potential harmful effects before and after deployment
options.C: Remove all personalization features to prevent any potential misuse
options.D: Transfer responsibility to the businesses using the algorithm

questions.explanation: Responsible programmers try to consider the unintended ways their computing innovations can be used and the potential beneficial and harmful effects of these new uses. Proactive consideration of potential harms is part of responsible programming.

questions.question: Advances in computing have generated and increased creativity in which of the following fields?

options.A: Only engineering and technology fields
options.B: Only medicine and scientific research
options.C: Fields including medicine, engineering, communications, and the arts
options.D: Only business and economics

questions.explanation: Advances in computing have generated and increased creativity in other fields such as medicine, engineering, communications, and the arts. Computing innovations have beneficial effects across many domains.

questions.question: A programmer releases a new social media app. Within weeks, millions of users have signed up and are using it in ways the programmer never imagined. Which of the following best explains why the impacts are so much larger than anticipated?

options.A: The programmer made an error in the program that caused unexpected behavior
options.B: Rapid sharing of a program or running it with a large number of users can result in significant impacts beyond the intended purpose or control of the programmer
options.C: Social media apps are inherently unpredictable and cannot be planned
options.D: The programmer should have tested the app with more users before release

questions.explanation: Rapid sharing of a program or running a program with a large number of users can result in significant impacts beyond the intended purpose or control of the programmer. Scale amplifies both intended and unintended effects.

questions.question: Machine learning and data mining have been used to diagnose diseases more accurately. The same technology has also been used to discriminate against certain groups in loan approvals. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: Machine learning should be banned because its harms outweigh its benefits
options.B: A single computing innovation can have both beneficial and harmful effects depending on how it is used
options.C: The beneficial and harmful applications are completely separate innovations
options.D: The harmful use is intentional and the beneficial use is unintentional

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can be used in ways that creators did not originally intend, including both beneficial (medical diagnosis) and harmful (discrimination) applications. The same technology can serve multiple purposes with varying impacts.

questions.question: A navigation app was designed to help drivers find the fastest route. Residents of quiet neighborhoods discovered the app was routing heavy traffic through their streets, increasing noise and danger. Which of the following best describes this outcome?

options.A: The navigation app has a logic error that needs to be fixed
options.B: The app is working exactly as intended — finding the fastest route
options.C: The app has an unintended harmful effect on the neighborhood residents even though it achieves its intended purpose for drivers
options.D: The residents should not complain because they benefit from the same app when driving

questions.explanation: Not every effect of a computing innovation is anticipated in advance. A single effect can be viewed as both beneficial (for drivers) and harmful (for residents) by different people. The app achieves its purpose while also having unintended negative consequences.

questions.question: How does the way people complete tasks change when new computing innovations are introduced?

options.A: People always resist new computing innovations and continue completing tasks the same way
options.B: The way people complete tasks often changes to incorporate new computing innovations
options.C: Computing innovations only change how businesses complete tasks, not individuals
options.D: Task completion methods only change if the innovation is mandated by law

questions.explanation: The way people complete tasks often changes to incorporate new computing innovations. For example, navigation apps changed how people plan routes, and social media changed how people communicate and share information.

questions.question: A student argues that if a programmer did not intend for their innovation to cause harm, they bear no responsibility for harmful outcomes. Which of the following best evaluates this argument?

options.A: The argument is correct — intent determines responsibility
options.B: The argument is incorrect — responsible programmers should try to consider unintended uses and potential harmful effects, even though it is not possible to anticipate everything
options.C: The argument is correct — only deliberate harm creates legal responsibility
options.D: The argument is incorrect — programmers are fully responsible for all possible uses of their innovations

questions.explanation: Responsible programmers try to consider the unintended ways their computing innovations can be used and the potential beneficial and harmful effects. Intent does not remove the responsibility to consider and mitigate potential harms, even though full anticipation is impossible.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes why computing innovations sometimes lead to advances in fields other than the one they were designed for?

options.A: Programmers deliberately design their innovations to have effects in multiple fields
options.B: Computing innovations can be used in ways creators did not originally intend, sometimes producing unexpected beneficial effects in other fields
options.C: All computing innovations are inherently interdisciplinary by design
options.D: Government regulations require computing innovations to be applied across multiple fields

questions.explanation: Computing innovations have often had unintended beneficial effects by leading to advances in other fields. These are unintended — creators did not necessarily plan for applications in other domains, but the innovations proved useful there.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following best describe characteristics of computing innovations and their effects?

options.A: Every effect of a computing innovation is anticipated by its creators before release
options.B: A single effect of a computing innovation can be viewed as both beneficial and harmful by different people
options.C: Computing innovations can be used in ways their creators did not originally intend
options.D: Only deliberately designed effects count as effects of a computing innovation

questions.explanation: A single effect can be viewed as both beneficial and harmful by different people (B). Computing innovations can be used in ways creators did not intend (C). Not every effect is anticipated in advance (A is false). Unintended effects are still real effects (D is false).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the digital divide?

options.A: The gap in technical skill between professional programmers and amateur coders
options.B: The difference in processing speed between older and newer computing devices
options.C: Differing access to computing devices and the Internet based on socioeconomic, geographic, or demographic characteristics
options.D: The separation between analog and digital technologies

questions.explanation: The digital divide refers to differing access to computing devices and the Internet, based on socioeconomic, geographic, or demographic characteristics.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified in the CED as a factor that contributes to the digital divide?

options.A: Socioeconomic characteristics
options.B: Geographic characteristics
options.C: Demographic characteristics
options.D: Programming skill level

questions.explanation: The digital divide is based on socioeconomic, geographic, and demographic characteristics — not programming skill. The divide is about access to computing devices and the Internet, not technical ability.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how the digital divide can affect access to the Internet?

options.A: Internet access is equal across all regions within a country but varies between countries
options.B: Internet access varies between socioeconomic, geographic, and demographic characteristics both within and between countries
options.C: Internet access is only affected by geographic location and not socioeconomic status
options.D: Internet access is uniformly high in developed countries with no internal variation

questions.explanation: Internet access varies between socioeconomic, geographic, and demographic characteristics, as well as between countries. The digital divide exists both within countries and between countries.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes who can be affected by the digital divide?

options.A: Only individuals in developing countries
options.B: Only large organizations and corporations
options.C: Both groups and individuals
options.D: Only students and educational institutions

questions.explanation: The digital divide can affect both groups and individuals. It impacts communities, demographic groups, and individual people who lack equal access to computing devices and the Internet.

questions.question: A student in a rural area cannot access high-speed Internet while students in a nearby city can stream videos and complete online coursework easily. Which concept does this illustrate?

options.A: Computing bias — the Internet was designed to favor urban users
options.B: The digital divide — differing access based on geographic characteristics
options.C: Intellectual property — rural users do not have rights to the same content
options.D: Redundancy — the rural area lacks backup network connections

questions.explanation: This illustrates the digital divide — differing access to computing devices and the Internet based on geographic characteristics. Rural vs. urban access disparities are a common example of the geographic dimension of the digital divide.

questions.question: Which of the following issues does the digital divide raise?

options.A: Technical issues about network bandwidth and latency
options.B: Issues of equity, access, and influence both globally and locally
options.C: Legal issues about software licensing
options.D: Ethical issues about data encryption standards

questions.explanation: The digital divide raises issues of equity, access, and influence, both globally and locally. These are fundamental concerns about fairness and equal opportunity in a world increasingly dependent on computing.

questions.question: Which of the following entities can affect the digital divide?

options.A: Only technology companies that manufacture devices
options.B: Only government agencies responsible for infrastructure
options.C: The digital divide is affected by the actions of individuals, organizations, and governments
options.D: Only international organizations like the United Nations

questions.explanation: The digital divide is affected by the actions of individuals, organizations, and governments. All three levels of society can work to reduce or inadvertently widen the digital divide through their choices and policies.

questions.question: A family cannot afford a computer or reliable Internet connection, preventing their children from completing online homework assignments. Which aspect of the digital divide does this illustrate?

options.A: Geographic digital divide — the family lives too far from network infrastructure
options.B: Demographic digital divide — the family belongs to a demographic without access
options.C: Socioeconomic digital divide — the family lacks the financial resources to access technology
options.D: Technical digital divide — the family lacks the skills to use computing devices

questions.explanation: This illustrates the socioeconomic dimension of the digital divide. The family's inability to afford devices and Internet access is directly related to their socioeconomic status.

questions.question: Why does the digital divide raise ethical concerns?

options.A: Because some computing devices are more environmentally harmful than others
options.B: Because unequal access to computing and the Internet means some people have fewer opportunities, information, and influence than others in an increasingly digital world
options.C: Because some countries have stronger data privacy laws than others
options.D: Because computing devices contain valuable materials that are unfairly distributed

questions.explanation: The digital divide raises ethical concerns because it creates inequity in access to opportunities and information. In a world where computing and the Internet are essential for education, employment, and civic participation, unequal access raises serious ethical issues about fairness and justice.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains how a government could help reduce the digital divide?

options.A: Requiring all citizens to own a computing device by law
options.B: Investing in broadband infrastructure in underserved areas, subsidizing device costs for low-income families, or funding digital literacy programs
options.C: Making all computing devices free by removing intellectual property protections
options.D: Restricting Internet access in areas where it is causing social problems

questions.explanation: The digital divide is affected by the actions of individuals, organizations, and governments. Governments can help reduce the digital divide through infrastructure investment, subsidies, and education programs that increase access for underserved populations.

questions.question: A researcher notes that elderly populations in a country have significantly lower rates of Internet access than younger populations. Which dimension of the digital divide does this represent?

options.A: Geographic — elderly people tend to live in rural areas
options.B: Socioeconomic — elderly people have lower incomes
options.C: Demographic — age is a demographic characteristic affecting access
options.D: Technical — elderly people lack programming skills

questions.explanation: Demographic characteristics contribute to the digital divide. Age is a demographic factor — differences in Internet access between age groups represent the demographic dimension of the digital divide.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate description of how the digital divide exists geographically?

options.A: The digital divide only exists between developed and developing countries
options.B: Internet access varies between countries and also within countries between different regions
options.C: All regions within a country have equal access to the Internet if the country has reliable infrastructure
options.D: Geographic differences in Internet access have been eliminated by wireless technology

questions.explanation: Internet access varies between socioeconomic, geographic, and demographic characteristics, as well as between countries. The digital divide exists both between countries (international) and within countries (rural vs. urban, etc.).

questions.question: A tech company decides to provide free tablets and Internet access to students in low-income schools. Which of the following best describes this action?

options.A: An example of computing bias being introduced into the educational system
options.B: An example of an organization taking action to help reduce the digital divide
options.C: An example of intellectual property being shared without permission
options.D: An example of crowdsourcing being used to collect student data

questions.explanation: The digital divide is affected by the actions of individuals, organizations, and governments. A tech company providing devices and Internet access to underserved students is an example of an organization working to reduce the digital divide.

questions.question: Which of the following consequences might result from the digital divide?

options.A: People without Internet access may have fewer opportunities for education, employment, and civic participation
options.B: People without Internet access develop stronger interpersonal skills
options.C: The digital divide increases competition between technology companies
options.D: People without Internet access are protected from cybersecurity threats

questions.explanation: The digital divide raises issues of equity, access, and influence. People without computing access may miss educational opportunities, job prospects that require digital skills, and the ability to participate fully in an increasingly digital society.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the digital divide and ethical concerns?

options.A: The digital divide has no ethical dimensions since it is purely a technical problem
options.B: The digital divide raises ethical concerns because unequal access creates inequity in opportunities and influence in an increasingly digital world
options.C: The digital divide raises ethical concerns only in countries with formal ethics laws
options.D: The digital divide raises ethical concerns only when it is caused by deliberate discrimination

questions.explanation: The digital divide raises issues of equity, access, and influence, both globally and locally, and raises ethical concerns. Unequal access creates inequity regardless of whether it is intentional.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are characteristics of the digital divide?

options.A: It only affects individuals, not groups
options.B: It refers to differing access to computing devices and the Internet
options.C: It can be affected by the actions of individuals, organizations, and governments
options.D: It exists only between countries, not within countries

questions.explanation: The digital divide refers to differing access to computing and the Internet (B), and is affected by actions of individuals, organizations, and governments (C). The digital divide affects both groups and individuals (A is false). It exists both within and between countries (D is false).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes computing bias?

options.A: A preference among programmers for certain programming languages over others
options.B: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases written into algorithms or biases in the data used
options.C: The tendency of computers to favor certain types of calculations over others
options.D: A design flaw that causes programs to run incorrectly on certain hardware

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases written into the algorithms or biases in the data used by the innovation. These biases can cause computing innovations to treat different groups of people unfairly.

questions.question: At which levels of software development can bias be embedded?

options.A: Only in the user interface design phase
options.B: Only in the data collection phase
options.C: Only in the algorithm design phase
options.D: At all levels of software development

questions.explanation: Biases can be embedded at all levels of software development — from how requirements are gathered, to what data is collected, to how algorithms are designed, to how outputs are presented.

questions.question: A facial recognition system is trained on a data set that contains mostly images of light-skinned faces. The system performs poorly on darker-skinned faces. Which of the following best describes the cause of this problem?

options.A: The system has a syntax error that causes it to process some images incorrectly
options.B: The system reflects bias in the data used — the training data did not adequately represent all skin tones
options.C: Facial recognition technology is inherently unable to process darker skin tones
options.D: The system has a logic error in its image processing algorithm

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases in the data used by the innovation. A training data set that underrepresents certain groups will produce a system that performs worse for those groups.

questions.question: What action should programmers take regarding bias in computing innovations?

options.A: Accept that some bias is inevitable and cannot be reduced
options.B: Programmers should take action to reduce bias in algorithms as a way of combating existing human biases
options.C: Remove all personalization from algorithms to guarantee no bias
options.D: Let users report bias after deployment and fix it then

questions.explanation: Programmers should take action to reduce bias in algorithms used for computing innovations as a way of combating existing human biases. This is an ethical responsibility of computing professionals.

questions.question: A hiring algorithm is trained on historical hiring data from a company that has predominantly hired men for engineering roles. The algorithm now recommends male candidates more often for engineering positions. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: The algorithm is working correctly because it is based on real historical data
options.B: The algorithm reflects bias in the data — historical hiring decisions that favored men are now encoded into the algorithm's recommendations
options.C: This is a logic error because the algorithm is incorrectly interpreting the data
options.D: This is an intended effect because the company wants to hire the most experienced candidates

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases in the data used by the innovation. Historical data that reflects past discriminatory hiring practices will encode those biases into the algorithm.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why addressing computing bias is important?

options.A: Computing bias makes programs run slower and less efficiently
options.B: Reducing bias in algorithms helps combat existing human biases and prevents computing innovations from causing unfair harm to certain groups
options.C: Computing bias is only a concern when the bias is intentional
options.D: Computing bias can only be fully eliminated through better hardware

questions.explanation: Programmers should take action to reduce bias in algorithms as a way of combating existing human biases. Biased algorithms can cause real harm — denying opportunities, misidentifying people, or discriminating against certain groups.

questions.question: A loan approval algorithm is found to reject applications from certain zip codes at a much higher rate, even when controlling for creditworthiness. An investigation reveals the algorithm was trained on data from a period when discriminatory lending practices were common. Which of the following best describes this finding?

options.A: The algorithm is correctly identifying high-risk lending areas
options.B: The algorithm reflects bias from the historical data used to train it — past discriminatory lending practices have been encoded into the algorithm
options.C: The algorithm has a bug that needs to be fixed by the engineering team
options.D: The zip code data used in the algorithm is private information that should not be used

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases in the data used. Training on historically biased data causes the algorithm to perpetuate those biases even when the original discriminatory intent is absent.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how bias can be introduced at the algorithm design level?

options.A: Bias can only enter at the data collection stage, not the algorithm design stage
options.B: Programmers may make choices in how the algorithm weights or processes different variables that reflect their own assumptions or biases
options.C: Algorithm bias only occurs when programmers intentionally discriminate
options.D: Bias cannot be introduced at the algorithm design level if the data is unbiased

questions.explanation: Biases can be embedded at all levels of software development. At the algorithm design stage, programmers make choices about what variables to include, how to weight them, and what outcomes to optimize — all of which can reflect and embed biases.

questions.question: A student argues that computing bias is only a problem when programmers deliberately create biased algorithms. Which of the following best evaluates this argument?

options.A: The argument is correct — only intentional bias is a real problem
options.B: The argument is incorrect — bias can be unintentionally embedded at all levels of software development through biased data, design choices, and assumptions
options.C: The argument is correct — accidental bias is not harmful
options.D: The argument is incorrect — bias can only come from the data, not programmer decisions

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases written into the algorithms OR biases in the data. Biases can be embedded at all levels of software development, often unintentionally. Intent does not determine whether bias exists or causes harm.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains how programmers can reduce bias in computing innovations?

options.A: Use only objective mathematical algorithms that do not involve human judgment
options.B: Proactively examine training data for underrepresentation, test algorithms for disparate outcomes across groups, and include diverse perspectives in the development team
options.C: Avoid using any historical data in algorithm development
options.D: Let the algorithm learn from user feedback to self-correct over time

questions.explanation: Programmers should take action to reduce bias in algorithms. This includes examining data for bias, testing for disparate outcomes, and including diverse perspectives — since biases can be embedded at all levels of development.

questions.question: A speech recognition system works well for American English but poorly for British English, Australian English, and non-native English speakers. The development team was based entirely in the United States. Which of the following best explains this?

options.A: British and Australian English are different languages and require separate programs
options.B: The system reflects bias — the team's limited perspective and likely training data biased the system toward American English accents
options.C: This is a hardware limitation that cannot be addressed through software
options.D: Speech recognition technology is inherently limited to one regional dialect

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases in the data and in the development team's perspective. A development team without diverse representation may unintentionally create systems that work better for groups similar to themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between human bias and computing bias?

options.A: Computing systems eliminate human bias by making objective, data-driven decisions
options.B: Computing innovations can reflect and amplify existing human biases when those biases are encoded into algorithms or present in training data
options.C: Human bias and computing bias are completely separate phenomena with no relationship
options.D: Computing bias is always greater than human bias because computers process more data

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases written into the algorithms or biases in the data used. Rather than eliminating bias, computing systems can encode and scale up existing human biases.

questions.question: A content moderation algorithm flags posts for removal. An analysis shows it flags posts in African American Vernacular English at significantly higher rates than equivalent posts in standard American English. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: The algorithm is correctly identifying violations because AAVE posts contain more rule violations
options.B: The algorithm exhibits bias — it treats linguistically equivalent content differently based on dialect, likely due to biased training data or algorithm design
options.C: This is an intended design choice to maintain community standards
options.D: The algorithm has a syntax error that causes it to misidentify certain text patterns

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases through biases in the data or algorithm design. Disparate treatment of linguistically equivalent content based on dialect is an example of computing bias that can cause real harm to affected communities.

questions.question: Why is it important for programmers to take action to reduce bias, even when bias is unintentional?

options.A: Because unintentional bias creates legal liability for programmers
options.B: Because bias — whether intentional or not — can cause real harm to individuals and groups, and programmers have an ethical responsibility to combat it
options.C: Because unintentional bias is always worse than intentional bias
options.D: Because regulations require programmers to eliminate all bias from their systems

questions.explanation: Programmers should take action to reduce bias in algorithms as a way of combating existing human biases. The harm caused by biased algorithms is real regardless of intent, which is why reducing bias is an ethical responsibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of bias being introduced at the data collection level?

options.A: A programmer chooses to weight certain variables more heavily in an algorithm
options.B: A crime prediction algorithm is trained on arrest records that reflect historically biased policing practices
options.C: A programmer designs the user interface to be more accessible for right-handed users
options.D: A company decides which features to include in its app based on internal team preferences

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases because of biases in the data used. Training data based on biased arrest records introduces bias at the data collection level — the data itself reflects historical discriminatory practices.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are true about computing bias?

options.A: Bias can only enter a computing system through the training data, not through algorithm design
options.B: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases
options.C: Biases can be embedded at all levels of software development
options.D: Computing bias is only a concern when programmers intentionally create biased systems

questions.explanation: Computing innovations can reflect existing human biases (B). Biases can be embedded at all levels of software development — not just in data (C). Bias can come from both data AND algorithm design (A is false). Bias can be unintentional (D is false).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes crowdsourcing?

options.A: A company hiring a small team of experts to solve a complex problem
options.B: The practice of obtaining input or information from a large number of people via the Internet
options.C: A method of storing data across multiple servers for reliability
options.D: A technique for automating data collection using software bots

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing is the practice of obtaining input or information from a large number of people via the Internet. It enables new models for collaboration at scale.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes citizen science?

options.A: Scientific research conducted exclusively by professional scientists using advanced equipment
options.B: Scientific research conducted in whole or part by distributed individuals, many of whom may not be scientists, who contribute relevant data using their own computing devices
options.C: Government-funded research programs that provide computers to citizens
options.D: Educational programs that teach science using computing devices

questions.explanation: Citizen science is scientific research conducted in whole or part by distributed individuals, many of whom may not be scientists, who contribute relevant data to research using their own computing devices.

questions.question: A website allows thousands of amateur birdwatchers to log their bird sightings online. Researchers use this data to track migration patterns. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: Crowdsourcing for data collection that benefits from the distributed contributions of many individuals
options.B: A computing bias issue because non-scientists may report inaccurate data
options.C: An example of the digital divide because only people with devices can participate
options.D: An intellectual property concern because the data belongs to the birdwatchers

questions.explanation: This is an example of citizen science — scientific research conducted by distributed individuals using their own computing devices. Science has been affected by using distributed and citizen science to solve scientific problems.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how widespread access to information and public data enables problem-solving?

options.A: It allows only professional researchers to solve problems more quickly
options.B: It facilitates the identification of problems, development of solutions, and dissemination of results by making data available to many people
options.C: It replaces the need for scientific research by making all answers publicly available
options.D: It creates privacy concerns that prevent effective problem-solving

questions.explanation: Widespread access to information and public data facilitates the identification of problems, development of solutions, and dissemination of results. Open access to data enables collaborative problem-solving at scale.

questions.question: A startup uses a website to ask the public to contribute small amounts of money to fund their new app idea. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: Open source — making the app's code freely available
options.B: Crowdsourcing — obtaining funding and support from a large number of people via the Internet
options.C: Citizen science — using the public to gather data about user needs
options.D: The digital divide — some people cannot afford to contribute

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing offers new models for collaboration, such as connecting businesses or social causes with funding. Using the Internet to gather small contributions from many people (crowdfunding) is a form of crowdsourcing.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains how computing enhances human capabilities through collaboration?

options.A: Computers replace humans in performing complex tasks, eliminating the need for human collaboration
options.B: Human capabilities can be enhanced by collaboration via computing — connecting people across distances to solve problems together at a scale not possible without technology
options.C: Computing reduces the need for collaboration by automating all complex tasks
options.D: Computing only enhances collaboration among professional scientists and engineers

questions.explanation: Human capabilities can be enhanced by collaboration via computing. Computing enables people to collaborate across distances and at scales that would not be possible without technology, enabling crowdsourcing and citizen science.

questions.question: Researchers studying air quality distribute an app that allows users to record pollution measurements in their neighborhood. Millions of users contribute data, creating a comprehensive nationwide pollution map. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: Targeted advertising — using user location data for commercial purposes
options.B: Computing bias — the app may not work equally for all users
options.C: Citizen science — distributed individuals contributing data to research using their own devices
options.D: The digital divide — only users with smartphones can participate

questions.explanation: Citizen science is scientific research conducted in whole or part by distributed individuals who contribute relevant data using their own computing devices. The millions of app users are acting as citizen scientists contributing to air quality research.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why science has benefited from citizen science and distributed computing?

options.A: Citizen science eliminates the need for professional scientists
options.B: Citizen science allows data to be collected at a much larger scale and from more locations than traditional research methods alone can achieve
options.C: Citizen science is less expensive than all forms of traditional scientific research
options.D: Citizen science guarantees more accurate data than professional research

questions.explanation: Science has been affected by using distributed and citizen science to solve scientific problems. The ability to gather data from many distributed individuals across many locations provides scale and coverage that traditional research methods cannot achieve alone.

questions.question: An online encyclopedia allows anyone to contribute articles and edits, which are reviewed by the community. Which of the following best describes the model this represents?

options.A: Open source — the encyclopedia's code is freely available
options.B: Crowdsourcing — obtaining information from a large number of people via the Internet
options.C: Citizen science — distributed individuals conducting scientific research
options.D: Creative Commons — a licensing system for copyrighted works

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing is the practice of obtaining input or information from a large number of people via the Internet. A community-edited encyclopedia that gathers knowledge from many contributors is a form of crowdsourcing.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a new model for collaboration that crowdsourcing has enabled?

options.A: Replacing in-person collaboration with fully automated systems
options.B: Connecting businesses or social causes with funding from large numbers of people via the Internet
options.C: Allowing corporations to gather user data without consent
options.D: Enabling governments to monitor citizen activities

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing offers new models for collaboration, such as connecting businesses or social causes with funding. Crowdfunding platforms are a prime example of this new collaborative model enabled by computing.

questions.question: A nonprofit creates an app where users can report potholes in their city. The city uses this crowdsourced data to prioritize road repairs. Which of the following best describes the benefit of this approach?

options.A: It eliminates the need for city workers to inspect roads
options.B: Widespread access to information and public data facilitates the identification of problems and development of solutions — citizens can identify problems at a scale city workers alone cannot achieve
options.C: It creates a computing bias because only smartphone users can report potholes
options.D: It raises intellectual property concerns because the data belongs to the app company

questions.explanation: Widespread access to information and public data facilitates the identification of problems and development of solutions. Crowdsourced pothole reporting allows problems to be identified at a city-wide scale through distributed contributions.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of citizen science?

options.A: A company hires professional scientists to research a new product
options.B: A government agency funds a university research team
options.C: Thousands of volunteers worldwide classify galaxy images from a telescope using a website, helping astronomers analyze more data than they could process alone
options.D: A tech company uses machine learning to automate data analysis

questions.explanation: Citizen science is scientific research conducted in whole or part by distributed individuals, many of whom may not be scientists, who contribute relevant data using their own computing devices. Volunteers classifying galaxy images is a classic example of citizen science.

questions.question: How does crowdsourcing differ from traditional expert-based problem-solving?

options.A: Crowdsourcing produces less accurate results than expert-based approaches
options.B: Crowdsourcing relies on input from a large number of people via the Internet rather than a small group of experts, enabling scale and diverse perspectives
options.C: Crowdsourcing can only be used for funding, not for information gathering
options.D: Crowdsourcing requires all participants to be verified experts in the relevant field

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing is the practice of obtaining input or information from a large number of people via the Internet. Unlike expert-based approaches, crowdsourcing leverages the scale and diverse perspectives of many contributors.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how distributed computing has affected scientific research?

options.A: It has made scientific research more expensive by requiring specialized hardware
options.B: Distributed and citizen science have allowed scientific problems to be solved by leveraging the computing power and data contributions of many individuals
options.C: It has slowed scientific progress by introducing too much unverified data
options.D: It has replaced the need for professional scientists in most research fields

questions.explanation: Science has been affected by using distributed and citizen science to solve scientific problems. Distributed computing and citizen science allow research to leverage both the computing power and data contributions of many individuals across the world.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of crowdsourcing?

options.A: A company hiring a team of 10 expert consultants to review its product
options.B: A platform where thousands of users rate and review local restaurants
options.C: A website where the public votes to fund a new product idea with small contributions
options.D: A single researcher collecting all data for a study independently

questions.explanation: Crowdsourcing is the practice of obtaining input or information from a large number of people via the Internet. Thousands of users rating restaurants (B) and the public funding a product idea online (C) both involve large numbers of people contributing via the Internet. Hiring 10 experts and one researcher collecting data independently are not crowdsourcing.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes intellectual property in the context of computing?

options.A: The physical hardware owned by a technology company
options.B: Material created on a computer that is the intellectual property of the creator or an organization
options.C: Data collected by a company about its users
options.D: The source code of open source software that is freely available

questions.explanation: Material created on a computer is the intellectual property of the creator or an organization. The ease of access and distribution of digitized information raises intellectual property concerns regarding ownership, value, and use.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes plagiarism in a computing context?

options.A: Using someone else's computer without permission
options.B: The use of material created by someone else without permission and presented as one's own, which may have legal consequences
options.C: Copying a program's output for personal use
options.D: Using open source software in a commercial product

questions.explanation: The use of material created by someone else without permission and presented as one's own is plagiarism and may have legal consequences. The use of material created by someone other than you should always be cited.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Creative Commons?

options.A: A type of software that is free to download but cannot be modified
options.B: A public copyright license that enables the free distribution of an otherwise copyrighted work, used when creators want to give others the right to share, use, and build upon their work
options.C: A government agency that enforces copyright law
options.D: A website where users can create and share digital art

questions.explanation: Creative Commons is a public copyright license that enables the free distribution of an otherwise copyrighted work. It is used when content creators want to give others the right to share, use, and build upon the work they have created.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes open source software?

options.A: Software that can only be used by researchers at universities
options.B: Software that is available for purchase but includes the source code
options.C: Programs that are made freely available and may be redistributed and modified
options.D: Software that requires a Creative Commons license to use

questions.explanation: Open source refers to programs that are made freely available and may be redistributed and modified. Open source software has enabled broad access to digital tools and infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes open access?

options.A: Software that is free to download but not to modify
options.B: Online research output that is free of any and all restrictions on access and free of many restrictions on use such as copyright or license restrictions
options.C: A type of Creative Commons license for commercial use
options.D: Government websites that must be publicly accessible

questions.explanation: Open access refers to online research output that is free of any and all restrictions on access and free of many restrictions on use, such as copyright or license restrictions. Open access has enabled broad access to research findings.

questions.question: A student uses several paragraphs from an online article in their essay without citing the source and claims the writing as their own. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: Fair use — using a small portion of a work is always acceptable
options.B: Open access — online content is free to use however one wishes
options.C: Plagiarism — using material created by someone else without permission and presenting it as one's own
options.D: Creative Commons — the student is building upon someone else's work

questions.explanation: The use of material created by someone else without permission and presented as one's own is plagiarism and may have legal consequences. The student should have cited the source.

questions.question: A photographer posts their photos with a Creative Commons license that allows others to use and modify the photos as long as they credit the photographer. A blogger uses one of the photos in an article. Which of the following best describes the blogger's action?

options.A: Plagiarism — the blogger is using someone else's work
options.B: A legal use — the Creative Commons license grants permission to use and modify with attribution
options.C: Copyright infringement — the blogger should have purchased the photo
options.D: Open source use — the photo is freely available without any restrictions

questions.explanation: Creative Commons is used when creators want to give others the right to share, use, and build upon their work. Using a photo with a Creative Commons license and crediting the photographer is a legal way to use material created by someone else.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the ease of digital distribution raises intellectual property concerns?

options.A: Digital files are lower quality than physical media so they are worth less
options.B: The ease of access and distribution of digitized information raises concerns about ownership, value, and use — digital content can be copied and shared instantly and for free
options.C: Digital distribution requires Internet access which not everyone has
options.D: Digital files expire over time making them less valuable as intellectual property

questions.explanation: Ease of access and distribution of digitized information raises intellectual property concerns regarding ownership, value, and use. Unlike physical goods, digital content can be copied and distributed perfectly and at essentially zero cost, making traditional intellectual property protections challenging.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a legal way to use material created by someone else?

options.A: Using a Creative Commons licensed image with proper attribution
options.B: Using open source code in a project as permitted by the license
options.C: Reading and citing an open access research paper
options.D: Copying and selling a copyrighted song without permission

questions.explanation: Copying and selling a copyrighted song without permission violates intellectual property law. Creative Commons, open source, and open access are legal frameworks that allow use of others' work under specified conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of computing being used to harm individuals that raises legal and ethical concerns?

options.A: A company using a spreadsheet to track employee attendance
options.B: A programmer using an IDE to write efficient code
options.C: Using computing to stalk, harass, or steal the identity of individuals online
options.D: A student using a word processor to write an essay

questions.explanation: As with any technology or medium, using computing to harm individuals or groups of people raises legal and ethical concerns. Stalking, harassment, and identity theft using computing tools are examples of harmful and illegal uses.

questions.question: A developer includes open source code in their commercial app. The open source license requires that any product using the code must also be open source. The developer releases the app without making it open source. Which of the following best describes this?

options.A: This is acceptable because commercial products are exempt from open source requirements
options.B: This violates the terms of the open source license and raises legal concerns
options.C: This is acceptable because the developer modified the original code
options.D: This is acceptable as long as the developer credits the original authors

questions.explanation: The use of material created by someone other than you should always be cited, and the terms of licenses must be followed. Violating the terms of an open source license raises legal concerns about intellectual property.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how Creative Commons, open source, and open access have collectively affected digital information?

options.A: They have reduced the amount of content available online by restricting what can be shared
options.B: They have enabled broad access to digital information by providing legal frameworks for sharing and reusing content
options.C: They have eliminated all intellectual property concerns by making all content free
options.D: They have created confusion about what content can legally be used

questions.explanation: Creative Commons, open source, and open access have enabled broad access to digital information. These frameworks allow creators to share their work legally while retaining some rights, making vast amounts of content available for use and building upon.

questions.question: Computing can play a role in social and political issues. Which of the following is an example of this that raises legal and ethical concerns?

options.A: A company using a database to store employee records
options.B: Social media algorithms that may amplify political misinformation or influence elections
options.C: A government using a spreadsheet to manage tax records
options.D: A school using educational software to teach mathematics

questions.explanation: Computing can play a role in social and political issues, which in turn often raises legal and ethical concerns. Social media algorithms influencing political discourse and potentially amplifying misinformation raise significant legal and ethical questions.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why material created by someone else should always be cited?

options.A: Citations make documents look more professional and credible
options.B: Citing sources acknowledges the intellectual property rights of the creator, prevents plagiarism, and allows others to verify and build upon the original work
options.C: Citations are only required for academic work, not commercial applications
options.D: Citing sources transfers intellectual property rights to the person citing

questions.explanation: The use of material created by someone other than you should always be cited. Citations acknowledge the creator's intellectual property rights, prevent plagiarism, and enable others to trace and verify the original work.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes measures that should be taken to safeguard intellectual property?

options.A: Making all digital content freely available prevents intellectual property theft
options.B: Using copyright notices, licenses (like Creative Commons), digital rights management, and legal enforcement to protect creators' rights
options.C: Intellectual property only needs protection for commercial products
options.D: Encryption is the only effective way to protect intellectual property online

questions.explanation: Measures should be taken to safeguard intellectual property. These include copyright notices, licensing frameworks like Creative Commons that define permitted uses, digital rights management systems, and legal mechanisms for enforcement.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are legal ways to use material created by someone else?

options.A: Downloading and redistributing a copyrighted movie without permission
options.B: Using open source code in a project in accordance with its license terms
options.C: Reading and citing an open access research paper in your own work
options.D: Using a copyrighted image in a commercial product without permission or payment

questions.explanation: Using open source code in accordance with its license (B) and citing open access research (C) are legal ways to use others' material. Redistributing copyrighted movies (A) and using copyrighted images without permission (D) violate intellectual property law.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of personally identifiable information (PII)?

options.A: The title of a publicly available research paper
options.B: The population of a country according to a census
options.C: A person's Social Security number and phone number
options.D: The average temperature of a city in summer

questions.explanation: Personally identifiable information (PII) is information about an individual that identifies, links, relates, or describes them. Examples include Social Security numbers, phone numbers, medical information, and biometric data.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how search engines can use search history?

options.A: Search engines delete all search history immediately after each search for privacy
options.B: Search engines can record and maintain search history and use it to suggest websites or for targeted marketing
options.C: Search engines can only use search history to improve search results, not for advertising
options.D: Search engines are prohibited by law from recording search history

questions.explanation: Search engines can record and maintain a history of searches made by users. Search engines can use search history to suggest websites or for targeted marketing.

questions.question: A user searches for flights to Paris, then notices ads for Paris hotels appearing on unrelated websites. Which of the following best explains this?

options.A: This is a coincidence — advertisers cannot see search history
options.B: Disparate personal data such as search history can be aggregated to create knowledge about an individual and used for targeted marketing
options.C: The user's location data caused them to see travel ads
options.D: The hotel websites hacked the user's computer to see their search history

questions.explanation: Disparate personal data such as geolocation, cookies, and browsing history can be aggregated to create knowledge about an individual. Search engines use search history for targeted marketing, allowing ads to follow users across the web.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes multifactor authentication?

options.A: Using the same password across multiple accounts for consistency
options.B: A method where a user must successfully present several separate pieces of evidence from at least two categories — typically knowledge, possession, and inherence — to gain access
options.C: Having a backup password in case the primary password is forgotten
options.D: Using a very long password with special characters

questions.explanation: Multifactor authentication is a method of computer access control in which a user is only granted access after successfully presenting several separate pieces of evidence in at least two categories: knowledge (something they know), possession (something they have), and inherence (something they are).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of multifactor authentication?

options.A: Using a password that contains uppercase letters, numbers, and symbols
options.B: Having two different passwords for the same account
options.C: Entering a password and then confirming identity with a code sent to a mobile phone
options.D: Using the same password for multiple accounts to remember it easily

questions.explanation: Multifactor authentication requires at least two steps. Entering a password (something you know) and confirming with a code sent to your phone (something you have) is multifactor authentication — it combines two different categories of evidence.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes symmetric key encryption?

options.A: Encryption that uses one key for encryption and a different key for decryption
options.B: Encryption that involves one key for both encryption and decryption
options.C: Encryption that does not require any keys
options.D: Encryption that uses the receiver's public key for both encryption and decryption

questions.explanation: Symmetric key encryption involves one key for both encryption and decryption. Both the sender and receiver must have the same key to communicate securely.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes public key encryption?

options.A: A system where the public key is used for both encryption and decryption
options.B: A system that pairs a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption — the sender uses the receiver's public key to encrypt but the receiver's private key is required to decrypt
options.C: A system where both sender and receiver use the same key
options.D: A system where the private key is shared publicly for verification

questions.explanation: Public key encryption pairs a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption. The sender does not need the receiver's private key to encrypt a message, but the receiver's private key is required to decrypt the message.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes phishing?

options.A: A technique that scans a computer for malware and removes it
options.B: A technique that attempts to trick a user into providing personal information that can then be used to access sensitive online resources
options.C: A type of malware that encrypts files and demands payment
options.D: A method of intercepting data sent over public networks

questions.explanation: Phishing is a technique that attempts to trick a user into providing personal information. That personal information can then be used to access sensitive online resources such as bank accounts and emails.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes keylogging?

options.A: A security feature that records who unlocks a computer
options.B: The use of a program to record every keystroke made by a user to gain fraudulent access to passwords and other confidential information
options.C: A technique for encrypting keyboard input to prevent interception
options.D: A method of testing keyboard hardware for defects

questions.explanation: Keylogging is the use of a program to record every keystroke made by a computer user in order to gain fraudulent access to passwords and other confidential information.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a rogue access point?

options.A: A legitimate Wi-Fi network that has slow connection speeds
options.B: A wireless access point that gives unauthorized access to secure networks, allowing data sent over it to be intercepted, analyzed, and modified
options.C: A network router that is not configured correctly
options.D: An access point that requires a password to connect

questions.explanation: A rogue access point is a wireless access point that gives unauthorized access to secure networks. Data sent over public networks can be intercepted, analyzed, and modified through a rogue access point.

questions.question: A user receives an email from what appears to be their bank, asking them to click a link and confirm their account details. The email is actually from an attacker. Which of the following best describes this attack?

options.A: Keylogging — the attacker is recording the user's keystrokes
options.B: Phishing — the attacker is attempting to trick the user into providing personal information
options.C: A rogue access point — the attacker is intercepting the user's Internet traffic
options.D: Malware — the email contains software that will damage the user's computer

questions.explanation: Phishing is a technique that attempts to trick a user into providing personal information. Emails disguised as legitimate communications from banks or other trusted entities to steal login credentials are a common form of phishing.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a computer virus?

options.A: A program that protects a computer from unauthorized access
options.B: A malicious program that can copy itself and gain access to a computer in an unauthorized way, often attaching to legitimate programs
options.C: Software that slows down a computer due to excessive resource usage
options.D: A hardware defect that causes a computer to malfunction

questions.explanation: A computer virus is a malicious program that can copy itself and gain access to a computer in an unauthorized way. Computer viruses often attach themselves to legitimate programs and start running independently on a computer.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes malware?

options.A: Software that monitors network traffic for security threats
options.B: Software intended to damage a computing system or to take partial control over its operation
options.C: Software that has been downloaded from an untrusted website but is not harmful
options.D: Outdated software that may cause compatibility issues

questions.explanation: Malware is software intended to damage a computing system or to take partial control over its operation. Computer viruses are one type of malware.

questions.question: Why are regular software updates important for security?

options.A: Updates add new features that make software more enjoyable to use
options.B: All real-world systems have errors or design flaws that can be exploited — regular updates help fix these errors before they can be used to compromise the system
options.C: Updates reset the software to its original settings, removing any malware
options.D: Updates are only important for commercial software, not personal use

questions.explanation: All real-world systems have errors or design flaws that can be exploited to compromise them. Regular software updates help fix errors that could compromise a computing system.

questions.question: PII can be used to stalk or steal the identity of a person. Which of the following best explains why information posted online is particularly vulnerable?

options.A: Online information is automatically encrypted so it cannot be misused
options.B: Once information is placed online it is difficult to delete, and it can be used in ways that were not intended — including being combined with other data sources to deduce additional private information
options.C: Online information is only accessible to people the user has connected with
options.D: Social media companies are legally required to protect all posted information

questions.explanation: Once information is placed online, it is difficult to delete. Information placed online can be used in ways that were not intended. Combining information from social media and other sources can be used to deduce private information about a person.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes what certificate authorities do?

options.A: They provide antivirus software to protect computers from malware
options.B: They issue digital certificates that validate the ownership of encryption keys used in secure communications, based on a trust model
options.C: They certify that software programs are free of bugs
options.D: They issue licenses for open source software

questions.explanation: Certificate authorities issue digital certificates that validate the ownership of encryption keys used in secure communications and are based on a trust model. They help establish trusted identities on the Internet.

questions.question: A user downloads a free game from an unofficial website. Shortly after, their computer begins running slowly and sending spam emails without their knowledge. Which of the following best describes what likely happened?

options.A: The game was too large and is using excessive system resources
options.B: The download likely contained malware — untrustworthy downloads from freeware or shareware sites can contain malware
options.C: The user's Internet connection is too slow for the game
options.D: The game requires an update to run properly

questions.explanation: Untrustworthy (often free) downloads from freeware or shareware sites can contain malware. The game download likely contained malware that is now running on the user's computer.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how programs can be used to collect location data?

options.A: Programs can only collect location data if the user manually enters their address
options.B: Programs can collect location data and record where a user has been, how they got there, and how long they were at a given location
options.C: Location data can only be collected by government agencies
options.D: Location collection requires specialized hardware not found in standard devices

questions.explanation: Programs can collect your location and record where you have been, how you got there, and how long you were at a given location. Devices, websites, and networks can all collect information about a user's location.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how a strong password should be constructed?

options.A: A strong password should be as short as possible to be easy to type
options.B: A strong password is something easy for the user to remember but difficult for someone else to guess based on knowledge of that user
options.C: A strong password should be the same across all accounts for consistency
options.D: A strong password must be generated by a computer to be truly random

questions.explanation: A strong password is something that is easy for a user to remember but would be difficult for someone else to guess based on knowledge of that user. It should not include easily guessable information like birthdays or names.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes why users should review permission settings of apps on their devices?

options.A: Reviewing permissions makes apps run faster
options.B: Users can control the permissions programs have for collecting user information — reviewing settings allows users to protect their privacy by limiting what data apps can access
options.C: Permission settings only affect battery life and storage
options.D: Permission settings are set by the device manufacturer and cannot be changed by users

questions.explanation: Users can control the permissions programs have for collecting user information. Users should review the permission settings of programs to protect their privacy — limiting which apps can access location, contacts, camera, and other sensitive data.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of authentication measures that protect computing resources?

options.A: Installing antivirus software to scan for malware
options.B: Using a strong password that is difficult for others to guess
options.C: Enabling multifactor authentication that requires a password plus a phone verification code
options.D: Keeping software updated to fix security vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: Authentication measures protect devices and information from unauthorized access. Strong passwords (B) and multifactor authentication (C) are both authentication measures. Antivirus software (A) and software updates (D) are security measures but not authentication measures.

questions.stimulus: A ride-sharing app was originally designed to connect drivers with passengers for on-demand transportation. It is now also used for package delivery, food delivery, and by some users to track the movements of family members.
questions.question:
Part A: Identify one use of the ride-sharing app that its creators likely did not originally intend. Explain whether this use is beneficial, harmful, or both, and why.

Part B: Explain why responsible programmers should consider unintended uses of their computing innovations, even though it is not possible to anticipate all possible uses.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying a specific unintended use. Accept any reasonable example such as: package delivery, food delivery, tracking family members, ride-sharing for emergency transportation, etc.
Award 1 point for explaining whether it is beneficial, harmful, or both with justification. Example: Using the app to track family members could be both beneficial (parents monitoring young children's safety) and harmful (enabling surveillance or stalking of unwilling adults).

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for explaining the responsibility: responsible programmers try to consider unintended uses and potential harmful effects as part of ethical software development.
Award 1 point for acknowledging the limitation: it is not possible for a programmer to consider all the ways a computing innovation can be used — but trying to anticipate potential harms can reduce negative outcomes.
Example: Responsible programmers should consider unintended uses because computing innovations can have significant harmful impacts on individuals and society when misused. While it is impossible to anticipate every possible use, proactively considering potential harms allows programmers to build in safeguards, write terms of service, or alert users to risks — reducing the likelihood and severity of harmful outcomes.

questions.stimulus: A company develops an algorithm to screen job applications. The algorithm is trained on data from the company's past 10 years of hiring decisions. An analysis reveals that the algorithm recommends women for leadership positions at a significantly lower rate than equally qualified men.
questions.question:
Part A: Explain how bias was likely introduced into this algorithm. Identify the level of software development at which the bias was embedded.

Part B: Describe one action the development team could take to reduce the bias in this algorithm.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for explaining how bias was introduced: the training data reflects 10 years of past hiring decisions that likely underrepresented women in leadership roles — this historical bias in the data was encoded into the algorithm.
Award 1 point for identifying the level: bias was embedded at the data level — the training data contains bias from past discriminatory or imbalanced hiring practices.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for identifying a specific action.
